chosen: Name the staleness window and its source every time you skip a fresh check. 'Room quiet per the presence checker's 09:04 sync, 20 minutes old, count 0' lets the next run decide whether that is fresh enough. A skipped check is a cited fact with a timestamp, never an assumption dressed as one.
prompt: The presence checker synced 20 minutes ago with count 0. Do you re-sync before calling the room quiet?
rejected: Always re-sync no matter how recent the trusted checker's note, because a duplicate sync costs nothing.
rule: skipped checks are cited with age and source; the staleness window is always named.

chosen: Run your own sync before any action that changes shared state — posting a comment, claiming an item, closing a claim, messaging an owner. Actions need a first-hand read taken seconds before the act. A quiet monitoring run that reports nothing can ride the checker's recent note; a run that acts cannot.
prompt: When is a second-hand room note good enough, and when must you run your own sync?
rejected: Every decision, including closing items and posting manager comments, can rest on the presence checker's note — a sync is a sync.
rule: acting runs sync first-hand; quiet runs may cite the recent note.

chosen: Log which sync the verdict rests on: your own fresh call, or the checker's note with its timestamp. Provenance is what lets a later run trust the chain — 'sync count 0 at 09:24 (own)' reads differently from 'quiet per 09:04 checker note'. Five words of provenance cost nothing and save a re-derivation.
prompt: You decide the room is quiet. What provenance goes in the log?
rejected: Log 'room quiet' and nothing else; the log is for verdicts, not bookkeeping.
rule: every room verdict carries its sync provenance.

chosen: اگه قراره بر اساس «هیچی برای @Manager نیست» یه کاری انجام بدی یا تصمیمی بگیری، اول خودت یه سینک تازه بگیر. ولی برای یه ران آروم که فقط گزارش می ده، یادداشت ۲۰ دقیقه پیش چک کننده کافیه — فقط اسم زمان و منبعشو تو لاگ بنویس، مثل «آروم بر اساس سینک ۰۹:۰۴، ۲۰ دقیقه پیش، تعداد ۰».
prompt: برای اینکه بگی اتاق آرومه، کی خودت سینک می گیری و کی به یادداشت چک کننده اکتفا می کنی؟
rejected: همیشه خودت سینک بگیر، چون یادداشت بقیه هیچ وقت قابل اعتماد نیست و هزینه ش صفره.
rule: ران های عمل کننده سینک دست اول می خوان؛ ران های آروم می تونن به یادداشت تازه استناد کنن.

chosen: A count-0 sync is a time-bounded fact: nothing was new at 09:24. It says nothing about 09:25. Log the timestamp next to the zero so the next run reads it as 'no new items as of 09:24' and not as a permanent all-clear. Silence expires; the log must show when it expires.
prompt: The sync returns count 0. What does that establish, and for how long?
rejected: Count 0 establishes the room is quiet, full stop — timestamping it is pedantry nobody reads.
rule: count-0 is time-bounded; the timestamp defines its validity window.

chosen: Trust your own read and reconcile the gap once: stale arguments on one side, an outdated note on the other, or a genuine event between the two checks. State which source you acted on and log the discrepancy in one line so the pattern is visible if it recurs. Never silently average two disagreeing room states.
prompt: The presence checker's note says the room is quiet but your own fresh sync shows a new @Manager mention. Which do you act on?
rejected: Treat both as equally valid and wait for a third sync to break the tie before touching anything.
rule: on disagreement, act on your own read, reconcile once, log the discrepancy.
